items.caption:
Welcome to CastZone — Where South Africa Fishes. 🎣

The modern home for SA anglers. Bass, saltwater, and specimen in one place. No global noise, no irrelevant content. Just South African fishing, on South African waters, by anglers who actually go.

Join free at castzone.co.za

The golden hour doesn't just apply to photography. 🌅

SA's best bite window opens at first light — you get roughly 45 minutes of prime activity before the sun hits the water and the fish go deep. Get to the bank before sunrise. Fish quietly. The fish that woke up before you are still feeding.

Tag a mate who's always late to the bank 👇

Think you've caught something special? 🏆

The CastZone Trophy Room is live — submit your best catch with a photo and claim your spot on the all-time leaderboard. Carp & freshwater, bass, and saltwater all have their own category. One photo, your name on the board.

Castzone.co.za → Trophy Room

The moon controls more than the tides. 🌕

Fish are most active during solunar major periods — when the moon is directly overhead or underfoot. A session timed to hit one of these windows can triple your catch count compared to fishing the same spot in a dead period.

CastZone has a free Best Bite Times tool on every venue page. Use it. 🎣

Vaal River – Parys 🏞️

If you haven't fished this stretch yet, it's on your bucket list. The yellowfish run from August to October is world-class — these fish hit a fly or spinner like freight trains. The water runs clear, the setting is beautiful, and it's one of SA's true fly-fishing gems. Accessible from Parys town.

Find it on The Map at castzone.co.za 🗺️

Polarised sunglasses will catch you more fish than any new lure. 🕶️

They cut surface glare so you can see structure, weed beds, shallow holding points, and fish that are completely invisible through bare eyes. Bass anglers use them for sight-fishing. Saltwater anglers spot feeding fish from the rocks. Non-negotiable once you've fished with a quality pair.

Summer topwater is SA's most exciting bass fishing. 💥

Frogs, buzz baits, poppers — work them parallel to reeds and weed mats in the first 45 minutes after sunrise from October to March. The visual explosions are addictive. Commit to the strike, don't rip the bait away early.

Early start + topwater = best morning you'll have this summer.

Clanwilliam Dam, Western Cape 🐟

Home to the Cape smallmouth yellowfish (Labeobarbus seeberi) — found NOWHERE else on Earth. Targeting these endemic beauties on light tackle or fly is one of SA's most unique fishing experiences. The dam also holds excellent bass on the rocky points and brush.

Details on The Map at castzone.co.za 🗺️

67 SA fishing venues on one interactive map. 🗺️

Dams, rivers, estuaries, and saltwater spots across all 9 provinces. Each venue has GPS coordinates, species list, permit info, bite times, and real member reviews. Province filters, water level overlays, nearby venues.

Open The Map at castzone.co.za and plan your next session.

Cold water carp bait 101 🎣

In winter, carp's metabolism slows. They don't need to eat much, so your bait needs to punch above its weight. Go smaller — a 14mm hookbait outfishes a 24mm in cold water. Go sweeter — custard, vanilla, and a drop of molasses travel further in cold water where scent disperses slowly. Fish slow, fish tight to features.

Galjoen — SA's most earned catch from the rocks. 🎣

SA's national fish demands patience, the right tide, and real local knowledge. Red bait or white mussel on a Cape rock ledge at dawn is pure magic. You can't rush it. You can't buy your way to it. Every galjoen you land feels earned.

Who's got one on their bucket list? 👇

Drop shot — finally landing in SA. 🐟

SA bass anglers are catching up to this technique fast, and for good reason. Overfished Gauteng dams need finesse. Keep the weight on the bottom, twitch just enough to move the tail, and dead-stick it when fish are present but not committing. Go lighter than you think on the hook — 6–10 lb fluorocarbon leader.

Vaal Barrage, Gauteng 🎣

Gauteng's all-season carp water. Big fish, heavy snags, proper specimen carp scene — this is where Gauteng anglers go when everywhere else isn't fishing. The 60-day Rand Water permit is worth every rand. Bank fishing with hair-rigged boilies, long nights, coffee, and a proper take at 2am.

Details on The Map at castzone.co.za

Mono or braid? Here's the simple guide. 🎣

Braid (8–15 lb) for bass: better sensitivity, longer casts, direct hooksets. Fluorocarbon leader on the end.

Mono (10–20 lb) for carp: the stretch absorbs the run, fewer thrown hooks in long fights. Braid + shock leader for distance casting on big dams.

Know when to switch — it changes your results more than a new rod will.

August to October is SA yellowfish season. 🪰

The Vaal, Wilge, and Mooi River systems are running clear, the fish are aggressive, and midday dry fly fishing is actually a thing. SA's equivalent of a trout season opener — except yellowfish fight harder and don't mind the heat. Book a guide, grab a 5-weight, and go.

Got old tackle collecting dust? 🎣

List it free on the CastZone Tackle Box — South Africa's fishing classifieds. No fees, no middlemen. Photos, price, location — buyers contact you directly on WhatsApp. Clear out the shed, fund the next trip.

Post your listing at castzone.co.za → Tackle Box

Switch to circle hooks for carp. ♻️

Fewer deep hooksets. Healthier fish. Cleaner releases. Rig them the same as a standard hook — the critical difference: DON'T STRIKE. When the fish moves away, just tighten and let the hook do its job. The corner-of-the-mouth hookset is almost guaranteed. C&R anglers in SA are switching fast.

Rietvlei Dam, Pretoria 🎣

Inside a nature reserve, carefully managed, with some of the best carp fishing in Gauteng. The setting is unlike any urban dam — wildlife, birding, pristine banks. A Tshwane/SANParks day permit is required. Worth every cent for the experience alone.

Details and GPS on The Map at castzone.co.za 🗺️

A sharp hook catches fish. A blunt one loses them. 🎣

Spend 10 minutes before every session: touch-test every hook you plan to use (should snag your thumbnail lightly). Swap anything blunt — they're cheap. Check your mainline for nicks from rocks or snags. Check your knots by pulling firmly. 90% of lost fish are a preparation failure, not bad luck.

Winter bass fishing 101 🐟

Bass don't stop feeding in winter — they just slow down. The fish move to deeper structure (5–8 m on main-lake points, channel edges, submerged trees). Go slow: shaky head, Carolina rig, drop shot. A 10-second pause after a bottom contact often triggers the bite. Forget the fast crankbaits until spring.

Hout Bay, Cape Town 🌊

Snoek season on the Cape Atlantic is a bucket-list experience. A ski-boat run out of Hout Bay in July into a baitball — Cape gannets diving overhead, snoek smashing jigs below. Add a sunset Cape Malay curry with your catch and you have the perfect Cape winter day.

Now that's fishing. 🎣

Night fishing unlocks a different game. 🌙

Grunter work the shallows after dark. Geelbek are bolder at night in the surf. Bass blow up topwater in dead-calm evening conditions from October to March. The fish that ignore your bait all day can eat it confidently at night.

Invest in a quality headlamp with a red-light mode (doesn't spook fish or your mates).

Why CastZone? 🎣

FishSA closed. Bass Fishing SA is quiet. The Facebook groups are fragmented and full of noise. 1.3 million South African anglers deserved something better — a modern, mobile-first platform built specifically for SA waters.

This is it. Register free and make it yours at castzone.co.za

Hook size matters more than most anglers realise. 📐

Carp on boilies: size 6 to 10 (wide gape or curved-shank). Bass on soft plastics: 1/0 to 3/0 EWG depending on bait size. Yellowfish on nymph: #10 to #14. Light tackle saltwater: circle 2/0 to 4/0.

SA anglers over-size constantly. Go smaller — hook-up rate improves every time. The fish doesn't care about the number on the packet.

Two knots every SA angler must know. 🪢

Palomar knot: the strongest all-round knot for braid and fluorocarbon. Never slips, never fails on the strike. Tie it before everything else.

Improved clinch knot: your backup for lighter mono when you're in a hurry. Five wraps minimum — less and it will fail on a big fish.

Learn both. Tie them in the dark. A lost fish from a bad knot is the most avoidable mistake in fishing.

Reading water is the most underrated skill in fishing. 🔍

Bass stack on the shady side of structure — points, fallen trees, dock edges. Carp follow the wind, feeding on the upwind bank where food collects. Yellowfish hold in the seam between fast and slow water. Saltwater fish cruise the same gutters on every tide.

Learn to read a body of water and you won't need a fish finder.

Loskop Dam, Mpumalanga 🏞️

One of SA's most underrated bass dams. Big water, rocky structure, and largemouth that don't get nearly as much pressure as the Gauteng dams. The bushveld setting is stunning — you're fishing between mountains with no city in sight. MTPA permit required. Worth the drive from Joburg.

Details on The Map at castzone.co.za

Your drag is set wrong. Here's how to fix it. ⚙️

A correct drag should slip at roughly 25-30% of your line's breaking strength. On 10 lb line: drag slips at about 2.5 kg of pressure. Test it by hand — pull your line and check. Too tight = the fish breaks you off on the run. Too loose = you can't drive the hook home.

Set it before every session. It takes 10 seconds and saves fish.

Barbel season is open the moment it rains. 🌧️

African sharptooth catfish (barbel) feed most aggressively during and just after summer rain — rising water, murky conditions, and the flood of insects and debris into the system trigger a feeding frenzy. Heavy mono, strong hook, smelly bait (offal, bloodworm, pilchard), and you're in business. Night sessions in summer are electric.

Why fluorocarbon leader changes everything. 🎣

Fluorocarbon is nearly invisible underwater — its refractive index is almost identical to water. On clear Gauteng dams where bass have seen every lure, dropping to a 6-8 lb fluoro leader can double your strike rate. It's also more abrasion resistant than mono on rocky bottoms. The cost per spool is higher but the difference on pressured fish is real.

Berg River, Western Cape 🎣

One of the Cape's best-kept fishing secrets. The lower Berg holds yellowfish and bass in the cooler months, while the estuary mouth near Velddrif produces steenbras, harder, and the occasional kob. The upper reaches near Paarl are clean, accessible, and beautiful in autumn when the surrounding vineyards turn.

Find it on The Map at castzone.co.za

How to hold a fish for a photo and release it healthy. 📸

Support the belly — never hold a fish vertically by the jaw for more than a few seconds (it damages the spine). Keep it low over the water in case it slips. Wet your hands first so you don't remove the slime coat. Have your camera ready before you lift it. Quick photo, back in the water, hold it upright until it kicks away.

A well-handled fish fights again another day.

Check your fishing line before every session. 🎣

Run your fingers along the first 2-3 metres. Feel for nicks, fraying, or rough spots from rocks and snags — even one nick can halve the line's breaking strength. If you find damage, cut it off and retie. Mono and fluoro should be replaced every 6-12 months even if unused — UV and heat degrade it. Braid lasts longer but check the first metre weekly if you fish structure.

Hartbeespoort Dam, North West 🎣

Gauteng's most accessible big water — and still producing good carp, bass, and tigerfish despite the pressure and hyacinth. The hyacinth mats are actually holding structure for bass in summer. Fish the edges of the mats early morning with a weedless frog and you'll get explosive topwater strikes. Permit from Harties municipality required.

Details on The Map at castzone.co.za

Fishing in wind — don't pack up, adapt. 💨

Wind pushes surface food and bait fish to the downwind bank. That's where the feeding fish are. Cast into the wind if you have to — the effort is worth it. On dams, the windward bank in summer heat holds the most oxygenated water and the most active fish. Bass and carp both respond to it. Most anglers move away from wind. Move toward it.

How to present carp bait properly on a hair rig. 🎣

The hair rig changed carp fishing because fish learned to blow out a hook hidden in bait. With a hair, the bait sits just below the hook on a short loop of line — the fish picks it up confidently, the hook is free to turn and catch.

Critical: the bait should sit 3-5mm below the hook bend. Too long = bad hooksets. Balanced hookbaits (critically weighted to near-neutral buoyancy) make it even harder for the carp to eject.

Wilderness Lagoon, Garden Route 🌊

One of SA's most beautiful fishing settings. The lagoon produces leervis (garrick), kob, and springer — all on light tackle in crystal-clear water. Early morning surface lures along the reed edges is fly-fishing level visual excitement. The town is worth the trip alone. SA's Garden Route has some of the most underexplored light-tackle saltwater fishing in the country.

Find it on The Map at castzone.co.za

Want to cast further? Fix your technique before buying a longer rod. 🎣

Most lost distance comes from releasing too late (casting at the water instead of the horizon) or overpowering the cast (which collapses the rod). Load the rod with a smooth acceleration, release at 1-2 o'clock, and follow through. Pendulum casting for surf anglers adds 30-40% distance once learned. A smooth 90g cast beats a hard 140g cast every time.

Bass spawn season in Gauteng dams is something else. 🐟

Each year from late September through November, largemouth move shallow to build nests — 0.5 to 2 metres deep on hard sandy bottoms near structure. Males guard aggressively and will strike anything that comes close. Sight-fishing to nesting bass is some of the most exciting freshwater fishing in SA.

Catch, photo, quick release — let them finish spawning.

The importance of a landing net. 🎣

Lifting a fish out of the water by the line stresses the mouth and hook hold — a big fish can tear free or the line can snap at the worst moment. A rubber mesh landing net (not the old knotted nylon) protects the slime coat, keeps the fish calm, and gives you time to unhook properly. Buy one. Use it every time. Lose fewer fish and release them healthier.

The CastZone Trophy Room leaderboard is live. 🏆

Who's on top right now? Carp & Freshwater, Largemouth Bass, and Saltwater — three categories, three all-time leaders. The current champions hold their title until someone submits a heavier verified catch.

Could your best fish be on that board? Submit a photo catch at castzone.co.za → Trophy Room. Every approved catch counts toward the all-time ranking.

Fishing pressure makes fish smarter. Here's how to beat it. 🎣

Overfished SA dams produce educated fish — bass that flinch from anything that looks wrong, carp that confidently eject rigs they've felt before. Beat it with: longer leaders, lighter line, smaller hooks, slower retrieves, natural colours, and fishing times when most people aren't there (early, late, midweek). The fish haven't moved. They've just seen everything.

Post-spawn bass recovery — fish with care. 🐟

After spawning, female bass are exhausted and thin. They're in the shallows, feeding hard to recover, and they're catchable — but they're also vulnerable. Keep the fight short. Use barbless hooks if you can. Hold them in the water to recover fully before releasing. The female bass you release today is protecting next season's fish. SA bass populations depend on every angler treating them right.

Ebenezer Dam, Limpopo 🎣

Limpopo's best bass dam and one of SA's most underrated. Big largemouth in impeccable water, surrounded by the Tzaneen tea and avocado farming country. The dam has classic bass structure — creek channels, submerged timber, rocky points. Less than a 2-hour drive from Pretoria and completely different fishing to the Gauteng metro dams.

Details on The Map at castzone.co.za

Why you should fish the last 30 minutes before dark. 🌆

The transition from daylight to dark is one of the most reliable feeding windows in freshwater and saltwater. Visibility drops, predators get confident, baitfish move to the surface. Bass smash topwater. Carp cruise the margins. Kob and leervis work the gutter edges. The fish that ignored you all afternoon come alive.

Don't pack up when the light fades. That's when it starts.

Choosing your first serious bass rod. 🎣

For SA conditions: a 6'6" to 7' medium-heavy fast-action spinning rod handles 90% of bass fishing — soft plastics, jigs, lighter crankbaits, topwater. Pair it with a 2500-3000 size reel and 15 lb braid + 10 lb fluoro leader. Budget R800-R1500 for a rod that'll last years. Abu Garcia, Shimano Catana, and Penn Pursuit are all solid entry-level options available locally.

The CastZone forum is free, forever. 🎣

No subscription. No paywall. Post a thread, share a spot, ask a question, help a beginner. SA angling knowledge has always been passed down mouth to ear on the bank — now there's a permanent place to write it down.

Join at castzone.co.za and add your voice to SA's fishing community.

Teach someone to fish this weekend. 🎣

The best thing you can do for SA angling is put a rod in someone's hands for the first time. A nephew, a friend, a colleague who's always been curious. You don't need perfect conditions or an expensive setup — a basic rod, a float, some worms, and the closest accessible water.

Every angler was a first-timer once. Pay it forward.
